jobs.title: Program Director- Targets
jobs.description:
Stratolaunch is a technology accelerator that engineers operationally realistic testing at Mach 5+. Our air-launched, Talon testbeds are reusable, cost-effective platforms that enable routine access to the hypersonic environment. We deliver flight data critical to validating system performance and achieving rapid technology deployment. Together with our customers, we drive innovations that are imperative to advancing national security.

To achieve these great efforts, Stratolaunch is seeking a Program Director with at least 20 years of relevant experience. This visible leadership role is responsible for the successful execution of complex, multi-disciplinary programs, including strategic planning, cross-functional team leadership, and is responsible for all aspects of program delivery and organizational growth. The role spans the design and development, manufacturing, and flight test of a fleet of expendable hypersonic targets. A candidate for this role must be comfortable leading cross-functional teams in a strong matrixed environment, driving the execution of a high-complexity technical project. A strong candidate will have a strong sense of urgency and will be able to make difficult programmatic decisions in an environment where not all the desired information is available.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Leadership
Lead strategic program initiatives and present clear and concise information in executive forums, customer engagements, and internal leadership meetings.
Mentor, coach, and develop program managers and team leads across the program.
Program Oversight & Execution
Oversee execution of multiple, concurrent programs with full responsibility for cost, schedule, technical performance, and customer satisfaction.
Own and maintain a positive customer relationship by producing results
Drive the adoption of advanced program management processes, tools, and best practices.
Make high-impact decisions affecting program direction, resource allocation, and risk posture.
Lead program forecasting and budgeting activities, ensuring accurate financial planning and alignment with organizational goals.
Manage revenue recognition and contract invoicing processes, ensuring compliance with accounting standards and timely billing.
Monitor and report on program financial performance, proactively addressing variances and risks.
Strategic Planning & Business Growth
Partner with executive leadership and department heads to define long-term program strategies, business plans, and growth opportunities.
Lead the development of new business proposals, capture strategies, and customer engagement plans.
Identify and pursue opportunities for program expansion, technology insertion, and process improvement.
Customer & Stakeholder Engagement
Serve as the primary point of contact for key customers, government agencies, and strategic partners.
Negotiate complex contracts, manage high-level customer relationships, and ensure alignment with customer objectives and expectations.
Risk, Compliance & Governance
Oversee program risk management, compliance, and governance activities, including classified program execution and security requirements.
Proactively manage risk by developing risk mitigation plans and driving technical risks to closure with a high sense of urgency
Ensure adherence to all regulatory, contractual, and quality standards.
Organizational Leadership
Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Lead cross-functional teams (engineering, operations, procurement, finance, legal) to ensure seamless program execution.
Champion overall team growth and development, including talent acquisition, onboarding, training, and professional advancement.
Develop and manage senior-level talent pipelines and succession planning to support long-term organizational objectives.
Promote team engagement, collaboration, and high performance through effective communication and recognition programs.
Implement organizational development initiatives to enhance team capabilities and drive business results.
Reporting & Communication
Provide regular, comprehensive program status reports and executive briefings to the C-suite and Board of Directors.
Communicate program vision, goals, and progress to internal and external stakeholders.
Travel
Domestic and occasional international travel as-required to support program and company objectives.

Qualifications

Required:

Minimum 20 years of progressive experience in technical and/or program management, with at least 5 years in a senior or principal-level leadership role within aerospace, defense, or high-technology sectors.
A strong sense of urgency, with the ability to make tough decisions in a technical environment
Demonstrated success managing large, complex, multi-disciplinary programs with annual budgets >$100M.
Extensive experience in aerospace program management, subcontracts and procurement, personnel management, aircraft systems, aircraft operations, launch vehicle integration, and ground systems.
Proven track record of technical leadership, including oversight of subcontractors and prototype/low-rate production.
Advanced risk management expertise and experience with classified programs.
Exceptional facilitation, negotiation, and executive communication skills.
Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to obtain and maintain a TS (Top Secret) security clearance.
Demonstrated ability to lead in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and drive organizational change.

Preferred

Boost-glide hypersonic vehicle technology and hypersonic vehicle development experience.
Experience working directly with government agencies, regulatory bodies, and major defense contractors.
Air-launch, launch vehicle, and/or aircraft integration program experience.
Large transport category or military aircraft operations experience.
PMP, PgMP, or equivalent advanced project/program management certification.
Experience with classified program execution and secure environments.

Required Computer Skills

Advanced proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)
MS Project and other advanced project management tools

Education

Bachelor’s degree (B.S./B.A.) in Engineering, Business Management/Administration, or related discipline from an accredited institution.
Master’s degree or higher preferred.
20+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

jobs.title: Coalition Manager - Government Affairs
jobs.description:
This newly created position is designed to help Gordian better manage its government and regulatory affairs portfolio by centralizing engagement with coalitions, interest groups, contractor and labor organizations, and other associations with which Gordian participates. The position is designed to be remote, and travel is required.

We are seeking a talented manager with a combination of government affairs expertise and some familiarity with government contracting processes. This individual will drive communication and engagement with key interest groups and coalitions to shape government policy around construction procurement, cooperative purchasing, and facility assessment and planning. He or she will be a direct report to the Vice President of Government and Regulatory Affairs, and will work closely with other senior leaders, directors and managers within this rapidly growing company.

The successful candidate will focus a great deal on government policy around Job Order Contracting (JOC) for public facility and infrastructure owners. JOC is a procurement method and construction process that helps federal, state and local governments, schools, hospitals, higher education institutions and others maximize efficiency, optimize cost savings, and increase construction quality. Since Gordian’s inception, research and development of JOC best practices is at the core of the business. Out of this research and development came the most comprehensive and detailed database of construction tasks and pricing in the industry, software specifically tailored for the JOC process, and field experts supporting JOC implementation at hundreds of government clients at the federal, state, and local levels

Gordian is not a construction contractor. Gordian is a consultant, helping clients understand needs about their physical assets and implement business process change before those clients hire contractors.

Primary Responsibilities

Develop and implement a comprehensive coalition engagement strategy in conjunction with Gordian leadership and other members of the Government and Regulatory Affairs team.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize external political associations, trade organizations, advocacy groups, and stakeholder networks that can advance organizational goals.
Serve as the primary representative to key coalitions, associations, and other stakeholder groups, including seeking positions on appropriate committees and working groups.

What You Will Do

The Associate Laboratory Directorate, Weapons Production (ALDWP), at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) enables credible and sustainable strategic deterrence for the nation through the production of plutonium pits, detonators, and other non-nuclear components, along with the necessary evaluation that ensures safe and reliable products. The directorate's programs support multiple aspects of the nuclear security enterprise (NSE) and national security mission, including plutonium processing and disposition, high explosives and non-nuclear component production, manufacturing for NASA deep space missions, surveillance, materials management, and waste operations. ALDWP must simultaneously expand capacity and mature rate production for pits and detonators, while continuing to build on its high-precision, high-quality manufacturing capabilities for non-nuclear parts fabrication.

The ADLWP Senior Directors office (Stockpile Production Management, ALDWP-SPM) ensures the effectiveness of the stockpile by providing key components and services with quality, reliability, and responsiveness. Stockpile Production Management supports and is responsible for the ALDWP production agency (PA) program office managing the NA-12 weapons portfolios in NA-121, NA-122 and NA-125 along with direct oversight of the weapon detonator production mission at Los Alamos National Laboratory. The ALDWP-SPM Senior Director organization scope includes enabling production of detonators, non-nuclear components, radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs), and surveillance (pits, detonators, actuators, RTGs). ALDWP-SPM also supports weapon production in various ways (i.e. Production Operations, Weapons Dismantlement & Disposition team, Product Maturation, Metrology, etc...). The organization provides guidance and leadership to each designated team to meet the production mission across ALDWP and ensure collaboration with other groups at LANL and sites across the complex.

The Senior Director for Stockpile Production Management (ALDWP-SPM) office is seeking highly qualified candidates at the Project-Program Director 4 (PPD 4) level to manage NA-12 program portfolios. The PPD 4 vacancies will serve as program lead for one of our NA-12 programs (e.g., Production Operations, W88/W93 Programs, B61 Program, and Stockpile Sustainment Surveillance), providing overall leadership and management for their assigned program portfolio. The PPD 4 will be responsible for program development and/or program management of their respective program to ensure the overall deliverables and outcomes of their program are successfully managed. The PPD 4 will be responsible for ensuring life cycle and annually based program resource loaded schedules are maintained or developed and that the schedules are managed and status on a routine basis with the appropriate level of Earned Value Management (EVM) rigor (including Enhanced Management Level A) as necessary. In conjunction with the use of EVM to manage our programmatic scope, the PPD 4 is expected to provide guidance and leadership to define and actively manage risks including the formality of dedicated Schedule Cost Uncertainty and Risk Analyses (SCURA). Active involvement and engagement with both internal and external program stakeholders are expected: Product Realization Teams (PRTs), Integrated Product Team (IPT) members, Project Teams (PTs), Federal Program Offices (FPOs), other M&Os [Design Agencies (DAs) and Production Agencies (PAs), e.g. LLNL, LANL DA, KCNSC, SNL], LANL line organization management.

Leadership

Knowledge of and demonstrated experience in developing, implementing, and enforcing governmental regulations related to implementing plans or programs to meet or exceed contractual requirements, performance measures, regulations, and laws, including the proven ability to do so while operating within a highly sensitive national security environment.

Our communities are consistently recognized as “Best Assisted Living”
by the people who matter most—our residents and their families. That recognition isn’t earned through marketing; it’s earned through the relationships we build and the care we provide every day.

At Morningside, our culture is the foundation of everything we do. We Build Trust, Lead by Example, Offer Compassion, Operate with Excellence, and Make Memories
in every interaction. These values guide how we care for residents, support families, and work together as a team.

Our goal is to create communities where residents experience purpose, connection, dignity, and joy—surrounded by meaningful relationships, engaging experiences, and a place they are proud to call home.

These are not aspirational statements, they are the standard we hold ourselves to every day, with every resident, family member, and team member we serve. We bring the fun to senior living and we take the work seriously. If you’re a leader who believes both are possible at the same time, we want to meet you.

Position Summary

The Executive Director is the most important leader in the community. The person who sets the cultural tone, drives operational performance, develops the team, and ensures that every resident experiences the quality of life they deserve. This is a role with full operational authority and accountability, supported by a Regional Director of Operations and Morningside’s corporate teams.

As Executive Director, you will lead all aspects of community operations: resident care and services, financial management, team development, sales and marketing, regulatory compliance, and community culture. Create and sustain a workplace culture where team members feel valued, residents feel known, and families feel confident their loved one is safe and celebrated.
Lead employee appreciation and retention programs that strengthen team cohesion, reduce turnover, and build loyalty to the community and the Morningside mission.
Champion Morningside’s BLOOM values and person-centered memory care philosophy, modeling the standard for how every resident is known, honored, and cared for as an individual.

Resident Experience & Care Quality

Oversee all resident services including admission, individualized service plan development, healthcare coordination, and ongoing care management, ensuring each resident’s dignity, independence, and quality of life is protected at every stage.
Collaborate with clinical leadership to maintain the highest standards of memory care quality, safety, and programming consistency.
Maintain an active, personal relationship with residents and families through regular engagement, council sessions, and responsive follow-through on concerns and feedback.
Ensure all services and interactions reflect Morningside’s commitment to person-centered care by meeting residents where they are, not where the schedule requires.

Financial Management & Business Performance

Develop, manage, and be fully accountable for the community’s operating and capital budgets, ensuring financial performance aligns with company goals and resident needs.
Monitor and analyze performance against budget; identify variances early and implement corrective action with confidence and transparency.
Manage FTE levels, staffing costs, and departmental expenditures to maintain sustainable operations without compromising care quality.
Identify and pursue opportunities to enhance revenue and reduce cost while preserving the resident experience.

Team Development & People Leadership

Recruit, hire, develop, and retain a high-performing, mission-aligned team across all departments, ensuring every associate understands and lives the BLOOM values.
Coach and develop department heads with consistent direction, honest feedback, and genuine investment in their professional growth.
Partner with the community’s ERAC (Employee Relations & Administration Coordinator) and Morningside’s corporate HR team on employee relations, performance management, and compliance.
Conduct or ensure completion of thorough and compliant onboarding, orientation, and ongoing training programs for all associates.

Sales, Marketing & Occupancy

Drive occupancy and revenue performance through active engagement in tours, family consultations, and prospect relationships, demonstrating Morningside’s care philosophy firsthand.
Partner with the sales and marketing function to develop and execute strategies for achieving and sustaining census targets.
Build and maintain relationships with referral sources, physicians, hospitals, discharge planners, and community partners to generate leads and grow the community’s presence.
Represent Morningside publicly as a credible ambassador of quality memory care, in civic organizations, healthcare networks, and local business partnerships.

Regulatory Compliance & Quality Assurance

Ensure full compliance with all applicable state and federal regulations governing assisted living and memory care operations, including DSS requirements (VA), COMAR (MD), and equivalent requirements in the applicable state of the MEM operation.
Maintain all required records, licenses, reporting, and documentation in accordance with company policy and applicable regulatory requirements.
Lead emergency preparedness, safety protocols, and ongoing quality improvement initiatives across all departments.
Ensure the physical environment, buildings, grounds, common areas, and resident spaces meets Morningside’s standards of excellence and regulatory requirements at all times.

What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate is an experienced, compassionate, and results-driven leader who thrives in the complexity of senior living operations and never loses sight of why the work matters.

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Gerontology, or a related field required; graduate degree a plus.
Minimum of 3 years of executive-level leadership experience in assisted living, memory care, or a comparable senior living environment.
Demonstrated track record of financial performance, team development, and operational excellence in a residential care setting.
Must hold or actively be pursuing an Assisted Living Manager (ALM) license in accordance with applicable state requirements. Licensure must be current and in good standing at time of hire.

Skills & Competencies

Strong financial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, forecasting, and analyzing performance metrics.
Proven ability to build trust-based relationships with residents, families, team members, and community partners, especially in emotionally complex caregiving environments.
Deep personal commitment to person-centered, dignity-driven memory care and the values that make it possible.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills with the ability to inspire and develop a diverse team.
Ability to operate independently while maintaining transparency and alignment with regional and corporate leadership.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and comfort with HRIS, scheduling, and community management software.
Multi-state senior living experience a plus; knowledge of applicable state regulations (DSS/VA, COMAR/MD) preferred.

What We Offer

Morningside Elite Management offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to recognize the importance of this role and invest in the people who lead our communities.

Annual performance bonus eligibility

Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance
401(k) with safe harbor employer match

$2,500 annual tuition reimbursement

At Morningside, we believe great care begins with great leadership. If you are a leader who sees beyond the operational demands of this role to the human impact it makes, on residents, families, and the team members who show up every day in service of others, this is where you belong.

What You Will Do

The Associate Laboratory Directorate, Weapons Production (ALDWP), at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) enables credible and sustainable strategic deterrence for the nation through the production of plutonium pits, detonators, and other non-nuclear components, along with the necessary evaluation that ensures safe and reliable products. The directorate's programs support multiple aspects of the nuclear security enterprise (NSE) and national security mission, including plutonium processing and disposition, high explosives and non-nuclear component production, manufacturing for NASA deep space missions, surveillance, materials management, and waste operations. ALDWP must simultaneously expand capacity and mature rate production for pits and detonators, while continuing to build on its high-precision, high-quality manufacturing capabilities for non-nuclear parts fabrication.

The ADLWP Senior Directors office (Stockpile Production Management, ALDWP-SPM) ensures the effectiveness of the stockpile by providing key components and services with quality, reliability, and responsiveness. Stockpile Production Management supports and is responsible for the ALDWP production agency (PA) program office managing the NA-12 weapons portfolios in NA-121, NA-122 and NA-125 along with direct oversight of the weapon detonator production mission at Los Alamos National Laboratory. The ALDWP-SPM Senior Director organization scope includes enabling production of detonators, non-nuclear components, radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs), and surveillance (pits, detonators, actuators, RTGs). ALDWP-SPM also supports weapon production in various ways (i.e. Production Operations, Weapons Dismantlement & Disposition team, Product Maturation, Metrology, etc...). The organization provides guidance and leadership to each designated team to meet the production mission across ALDWP and ensure collaboration with other groups at LANL and sites across the complex.

Facilitate communication and problem resolution in addressing academic-related concerns identified by students and/or their professors;
Respond to student grievances in accordance with established school and university policies.

Design, implement and maintain systems and procedures for working with students at academic risk:

Oversee implementation of academic standards including development of academic probation contracts;
Direct academic affairs administrators and administrative support staff in tracking and notification of students with low GPAs, students on probation or at-risk within the MSW program;
Oversee processes around allegations of plagiarism and other forms of academic dishonesty and interpret policy and procedures, collect and file forms and evidence of plagiarism, refer egregious or repeat offenders to the Academic Standards Committee, consistent with School and University policies;
Provide leadership to faculty, academic advisors, and the practicum education department around policies and procedures in the School of Social Work related to academic standards within the BSW and MSW programs;
Develop and implement protocols to identify academically at-risk students to promote positive student outcomes.

Provide leadership in the delivery of a coherent and integrated explicit and implicit curriculum for class and practicum education;
Consult with Curriculum Committee on curriculum implementation, curriculum renewal, and adjunct faculty development;
Plan course offerings for all program sites within established time frames and in accordance with policy and procedures provided by the Office of the Provost and University Registrar;
Consult with faculty around course assignments and assign faculty to classes, collaborating with Center Coordinators and other stakeholders as necessary;

Provide leadership around licensing preparation and outcomes associated with the implicit and explicit curriculum and work with faculty to integrate licensing preparation within the curriculum.

Student Advisement And Registration

Direct the academic affairs administrative team to prepare and disseminate program and advisement materials to support academic advisement processes that are responsive to the differential needs of the School’s diverse student body;
Direct academic affairs administrators, center coordinators, and practicum education administrators to implement advisement and registration procedures;
Liaison with University offices to assure integrity of registration processes and implementation of student academic affairs policies and processes;
Direct academic affairs administrators and administrative support staff to ensure compliance with academic clearance processes for graduation from the MSW program.

Student Affairs

Supervise and collaborate with administration and faculty to promote opportunities for student participation in formulating and modifying policies affecting academic and student affairs.
Coordinate academic supports through external (University) resources for BSW and MSW students (e.g., Student Access, Counseling Services, writing and statistic tutors, career services).

Serve as the visible, accessible leader for residents, families, associates, and community partners by maintaining an open presence on the floor and throughout the community.
Create and sustain a workplace culture where team members feel valued, residents feel known, and families feel confident their loved one is safe and celebrated.
Lead employee appreciation and retention programs that strengthen team cohesion, reduce turnover, and build loyalty to the community and the Morningside mission.
Champion Morningside’s BLOOM values and person-centered memory care philosophy, modeling the standard for how every resident is known, honored, and cared for as an individual.

Resident Experience & Care Quality

Oversee all resident services including admission, individualized service plan development, healthcare coordination, and ongoing care management, ensuring each resident’s dignity, independence, and quality of life is protected at every stage.
Collaborate with clinical leadership to maintain the highest standards of memory care quality, safety, and programming consistency.
Maintain an active, personal relationship with residents and families through regular engagement, council sessions, and responsive follow-through on concerns and feedback.
Ensure all services and interactions reflect Morningside’s commitment to person-centered care by meeting residents where they are, not where the schedule requires.

Financial Management & Business Performance

Develop, manage, and be fully accountable for the community’s operating and capital budgets, ensuring financial performance aligns with company goals and resident needs.
Monitor and analyze performance against budget; identify variances early and implement corrective action with confidence and transparency.
Manage FTE levels, staffing costs, and departmental expenditures to maintain sustainable operations without compromising care quality.
Identify and pursue opportunities to enhance revenue and reduce cost while preserving the resident experience.

Team Development & People Leadership

Recruit, hire, develop, and retain a high-performing, mission-aligned team across all departments, ensuring every associate understands and lives the BLOOM values.
Coach and develop department heads with consistent direction, honest feedback, and genuine investment in their professional growth.
Partner with the community’s ERAC (Employee Relations & Administration Coordinator) and Morningside’s corporate HR team on employee relations, performance management, and compliance.
Conduct or ensure completion of thorough and compliant onboarding, orientation, and ongoing training programs for all associates.

Sales, Marketing & Occupancy

Drive occupancy and revenue performance through active engagement in tours, family consultations, and prospect relationships, demonstrating Morningside’s care philosophy firsthand.
Partner with the sales and marketing function to develop and execute strategies for achieving and sustaining census targets.
Build and maintain relationships with referral sources, physicians, hospitals, discharge planners, and community partners to generate leads and grow the community’s presence.
Represent Morningside publicly as a credible ambassador of quality memory care, in civic organizations, healthcare networks, and local business partnerships.

Regulatory Compliance & Quality Assurance

Ensure full compliance with all applicable state and federal regulations governing assisted living and memory care operations, including DSS requirements (VA), COMAR (MD), and equivalent requirements in the applicable state of the MEM operation.
Maintain all required records, licenses, reporting, and documentation in accordance with company policy and applicable regulatory requirements.
Lead emergency preparedness, safety protocols, and ongoing quality improvement initiatives across all departments.
Ensure the physical environment, buildings, grounds, common areas, and resident spaces meets Morningside’s standards of excellence and regulatory requirements at all times.

What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate is an experienced, compassionate, and results-driven leader who thrives in the complexity of senior living operations and never loses sight of why the work matters.

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Gerontology, or a related field required; graduate degree a plus.
Minimum of 3 years of executive-level leadership experience in assisted living, memory care, or a comparable senior living environment.
Demonstrated track record of financial performance, team development, and operational excellence in a residential care setting.
Must hold or actively be pursuing an Assisted Living Manager (ALM) license in accordance with applicable state requirements. Licensure must be current and in good standing at time of hire.

Skills & Competencies

Strong financial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, forecasting, and analyzing performance metrics.
Proven ability to build trust-based relationships with residents, families, team members, and community partners, especially in emotionally complex caregiving environments.
Deep personal commitment to person-centered, dignity-driven memory care and the values that make it possible.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills with the ability to inspire and develop a diverse team.
Ability to operate independently while maintaining transparency and alignment with regional and corporate leadership.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and comfort with HRIS, scheduling, and community management software.
Multi-state senior living experience a plus; knowledge of applicable state regulations (DSS/VA, COMAR/MD) preferred.

What We Offer

Morningside Elite Management offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to recognize the importance of this role and invest in the people who lead our communities.

Annual performance bonus eligibility
